caseno: Civil Petition For Leave To Appeal No. 572 of 1994
lawyer:
Mr. A. Baset Majumder, Advocate-on-Record ----- For the Petitioner. 
Mr. A. B. M. Khairul Huq Advocate instructed by Mr. Mvi. Md. Wahidullah, Advocate-on-Record ----- For Respondent No. 1. 
Respondent No. 2: Not represented.
parties:
Md. Mozammel Hoque ----- Petitioner
Vs.
Sonali Bank and another ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
Mustafa Kamal, J: The petitioner was defendant No. 2 in Mortgage Suit No. 83 of 1986 filed by the respondent Sonali Bank before the learned Subordinate Judge and Artha Rin Adalat, Rajshahi. The suit was for realisation of a loan given by the respondent Bank to a partnership firm of which the petitioner and defendant No.1 were partners. The mortgage suit was decreed on 23-10-90. But the petitioner did not receive the notice of the suit and came to know of the decree from a Notification published in the newspaper on 1-8-91, almost 10 months after the decree. The petitioner thereafter filed O. C. Suit No. 173 of 1992 against the said plaintiff and the partnership firm represented by the other partner with a prayer for declaration of the said decree as fraudulent and collusive. He then filed an application for stay of further proceedings in Artha Rin Adalat Execution Case No. 5 of 1992 on 6-1-93, but although he obtained an ad-interim order of stay in his favour, after final hearing on 30-3-94 the prayer for stay of the execution case was rejected against which the petitioner moved a revisional application, Civil Order No. 1667 of 1994, before the High Court Division, which having been rejected summarily by judgment and order dated 3-7-94, the plaintiff-petitioner in O. C. Suit No. 173 of 1992 seeks leave to appeal there from. 

 2. It is submitted by Mr. A. Baset Majumder, learned Advocate-on-Record for the petitioner, that the High Court Division erred in law in holding that the petitioner having failed to file a review application or an appeal against the decree within the statutory period and having not availed of the special remedy provided for in the Artha Rin Adalat Act cannot challenge that decree in a separate suit. He submits that the petitioner was a resident of Dhaka and the mortgage suit was filed in Rajshahi and he received no notice of the suit. He came to know of the decree after 10 months when all his remedies under the Artha Rin Adalat Act were barred. He therefore had no other remedy but to tile civil suit for getting rid of the decree passed against him. If in the meantime the decree is executed the petitioner will suffer irreparable loss and injury and his entire suit will be an exercise in futility. 

 3. In the facts and circumstances of the case, if the petitioner's allegation of non-service of summons of the suit is correct, his remedy of a separate suit is not barred, provided his remedies under the Artha Rin Adalat Act stood barred at the time of the filing of the suit for no fault of his own. But these are matters of evidence and nitil the plaintiff-petitioner proves these allegations in the suit the decree holder respondent-Bank cannot be denied the fruit of its decree for an indefinite period.
